transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05 15:00 UTC, Duration: 42 minutes, Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Sundial - Head of Search), Derek Alvarez (Sundial - Staff ML), Priya Patel (Sundial - Security)

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings endpoint + rerank endpoint for Sundial's clinical search product. Covered vector sizes, latency/cost tradeoffs, security concerns for PHI, and pilot next steps. Demoed a live query -> candidate retrieval -> rerank chain in Redwood Console and via the API.

Topics:
- Embeddings dimension and model choice
- Candidate generation vs. model-based rerank
- Latency and batch sizing recommendations
- Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO, data retention
- Pilot scope and KPIs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Morning everyone, thanks for joining. Alex from Redwood, i'll hand it to Priya in a sec for the demo. quick intro - we're going to show embeddings + a hosted rerank endpoint, and how the console helps you iterate.
[00:18] Maya (Sundial): Hi all, maya here. want to see end-to-end — especially how rerank affects clinical relevance and latency. we have PHI concerns so security stuff is big.
[00:27] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, thanks maya. quick agenda: show the embeddings API call, candidate generation approach (vector search), then our rerank endpoint that accepts candidates and returns scores. i'll also flip to the console and Optimize suggestions.
[00:45] Derek (Sundial): Is the rerank model hosted inside Redwood or do we run that ourselves? latency implications?
[00:55] Priya: Good q. rerank can run in our hosted path — it's a lightweight transformer that scores candidates. it's colocated with vector search in hosted mode to keep hops low. you can also bring your own reranker if you want Dedicated or Private.
[01:10] Maya: For us, throughput is moderate but p95 latency matters for clinicians. accepting 200-300ms is ok, under 500 absolute max.
[01:22] Alex: Noted. we usually recommend a hybrid: use the embeddings + vector DB for broad recall, then rerank top N (like top 30) to keep latency predictable. that typically keeps p95 in the 150-350ms range depending on model size and batching.
[01:40] Priya: I'm going to open the Console. (screen share) you'll see the embeddings catalog — for clinical content we'd suggest a 768 or 1024-d model tuned for medical semantics, but we can show a 768 demo for speed.
[02:05] [Priya shares sample API request]
[02:10] Priya: embeddings endpoint call. note the payload length, and we set batch_size to 16 in this demo. server returns 768-d vectors. minor transcription: it sometimes writes 'seven sixty eight' in the logs but it's 768 floats.
[02:28] Derek: Are those dense float vectors or quantized?
[02:31] Priya: Hosted returns float32 by default. we support quantized variants (int8) on select model profiles to cut memory and cost; Redwood Optimize suggests quantization levels based on your workload.
[02:47] Maya: How about the similarity function? cosine vs dot? we're using cosine now but want to understand expected hit-rate changes.
[02:55] Priya: We support cosine and dot. in practice cosine with normalized vectors works well for semantic similarity, but if you use rerank after candidate generation the absolute retrieval metric matters less — rerank is tolerant as long as you have high recall in candidates.
[03:10] Alex: i'll interrupt — important for indexing: prefix caching and K V cache behaviors reduce cost when you have repeated prefixes in queries, but for retrieval pipelines it mainly helps in generated text flows.
[03:26] Maya: ok, demo the rerank?
[03:28] Priya: yes. switching to the rerank example. the rerank endpoint receives candidate ids + their embeddings and the query, runs a model and returns scores and reasons if you enable structured output. here's a sample request we run in the notebook.
[03:45] [Priya runs notebook: candidate gen -> rerank]
[04:02] Priya: You can see top-5 before and after rerank — ordering changes for clinical context. notice one candidate moves up because the reranker picks up negation and context.
[04:20] Derek: That was neat. what's the per-call token cost and compute? If we rerank 30 candidates with a medium reranker what's the cost profile?
[04:29] Alex: Cost depends on model size and quantization. rough ballpark: reranking 30 candidates with a mid-size model is ~0.3-0.6 cents per query on hosted depending on sequence length; embeddings cost is separate. we can produce a detailed run cost estimate for your expected qps.
[04:47] Maya: We really need EU data residency for some pilot users — can hosted accommodate that?
[04:52] Alex: Yes, we have regional hosting options. for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private; but hosted can be pinned to cloud regions in EU depending on availability.
[05:05] Priya: Also security: SOC2 is standard; we integrate with KMS for key management and support SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. Priya Patel, are you on the call?
[05:18] Priya P (Sundial): yes. biggest question: PHI transit and storage — is data encrypted at rest, and can we enforce zero retention for hosted?
[05:27] Alex: Data is encrypted at rest and in transit. hosted mode by default retains short-term logs for debugging but we can set strict retention policies and offer Dedicated/Private if zero-retention is a hard requirement. we also support BYOK via KMS/HSM for Private deployments.
[05:44] Derek: For pilot, we'd like to try hosted first to iterate, then evaluate Dedicated if we hit policy gates.
[05:50] Alex: sounds reasonable. we often run short pilots on hosted with encryption + strict retention settings, then move to Dedicated for production.
[06:02] Maya: Priya mentioned Optimize — what suggestions would we get automatically?
[06:06] Priya: Optimize looks at your request patterns and suggests batching sizes, prefix caching, model quantization, and candidate N for rerank to balance lat/cost. i'll show a quick Optimize report from a synthetic workload.
[06:20] [Priya opens Optimize report]
[06:27] Priya: Here's a suggestion: reduce embedding dimension to 768 and enable int8 quantization for embeddings store; lower rerank model to small-medium and increase candidate N to 50 to improve recall then prune with rerank — it's a tradeoff but Optimize shows expected cost delta.
[06:48] Maya: We worry about hallucinations for clinical answers — does rerank reduce that?
[06:53] Priya: Rerank helps by prioritizing better-grounded candidates; for generative completions you should also use grounding documents and structured outputs. we can tie rerank scores to quality alerts in Console so you get regression alerts if rerank performance drops.
[07:08] Derek: Integration — we use a combined flow: vector DB for large-scale index, Redwood for rerank + hosted embeddings. How do you handle candidate storage? do we need to migrate index?
[07:18] Alex: You can keep your vector store and call rerank with candidate payloads, or host embeddings in Redwood's managed vector index for convenience. many customers run hybrid: your vector DB for indexing and Redwood for embeddings + rerank.
[07:34] Maya: Are there pre-built connectors to common vector DBs?
[07:38] Priya: Yes, we have connectors and quickstart scripts for Pinecone, Milvus, OpenSearch, but we also recommend using our embeddings store when you want simplified ops.
[07:50] [Interruption / phone beep]
[07:58] Maya: quick more on metrics — we want precision@5 and p95 latency targets in pilot. target precision@5 improvement of >12% vs baseline.
[08:08] Priya: ok noted. we can instrument token-level cost + per-route latency in Console.
[08:15] Derek: On the API side: what's the rerank payload size limit? in our flow we may send embeddings for 100 candidates in worst case.
[08:23] Priya: The hosted API supports payloads up to a few MB. for large candidate sets we suggest sending candidate ids and let Redwood fetch embeddings from managed store, or use chunked calls. sending 100 candidates with 768-d vectors is heavy; we suggest top 30-50 for practical latency.
[08:44] Maya: any limitations on structured output for rerank explanations?
[08:47] Priya: You can request structured reasons but it adds compute; we return either a scalar score or a small JSON of signals. sometimes the transcript labels them weirdly — we've seen 'reason tokens' show up in logs as 'reson tokens' but it's the same field.
[09:06] Alex: let's pivot to a short live benchmark — Priya will run a 500-query synthetic bench against hosted embeddings+r erank with small model and show p50/p95.
[09:16] [Priya runs benchmark - timer noise, typing sounds]
[10:02] Priya: Results are in: p50 ~ 110ms, p95 ~ 320ms for top-30 rerank on this synthetic workload. cost per query estimated at ~0.45 cents with current profile. (note: synthetic data optimistic vs real clinical documents).
[10:20] Derek: realistic numbers. can we customize retry/backoff and fallback policies? if rerank fails do we return candidate list?
[10:28] Alex: yes — Redwood supports fallback to candidate-only results, and you can define routes with policy-based fallback by model family or region. there is an automatic degrade to a smaller model if latency spikes.
[10:44] Priya: switching back to Console to show tracing; you can see token-level traces, request id, and the rerank scoring trace for each candidate.
[10:58] [screen share: Console traces - small text, some mis-read acronyms]
[11:12] Maya: security again: can we get a penetration test report?
[11:16] Alex: we have penetration test summaries and can coordinate an NDA'd report exchange. we'll include that in the security pack.
[11:24] Priya P: SAML mapping and RBAC — can we get role constraints so only analytics team can run bulk exports?
[11:30] Alex: yes, RBAC in Console supports roles & scoped permissions; you can also integrate with your IdP for SAML attribute mappings.
[11:40] Derek: developer ergonomics — SDKs look good. are there examples in python and go?
[11:44] Priya: yes, python, node, java are supported; we also have a quickstart repo that sets up the rerank pipeline. i'll share the link.
[11:52] Maya: Regarding pilot timeline — we aim to run a 3-week pilot in Jan. need to confirm cost and SOW.
[12:00] Alex: we can draft a pilot SOW: objectives, dataset, KPIs, cost estimate for hosted pilot with an option to move to Dedicated.
[12:10] Derek: ok. small thing — latency in EU region vs US, any estimates?
[12:15] Priya: EU region adds usually 20-40ms network; p95 shifts accordingly. Dedicated in-region reduces that.
[12:24] Maya: any note about logging PII in Console — can we mask PII in traces?
[12:29] Alex: there's redaction support and on ingest masking rules; we can apply regex-based redaction in the pipeline.
[12:38] Priya: quick question from my side — what's your target qps for pilot?
[12:41] Maya: 5 qps sustained, with spikes to 20 qps during peak hours.
[12:47] Priya: that's small, easily covered on hosted during pilot; Dedicated reserved capacity if you want hard SLAs.
[12:56] [Small side chatter, smiles]
[13:05] Priya: i'll summarize the recommended configuration for pilot: embeddings model (768-d) hosted in EU region, int8 quantized embeddings store, candidate N=50, rerank top 30 with a small-medium reranker, retention policy short (7 days) for logs, KMS for keys.
[13:25] Maya: sounds good. can you also include sample surge handling? we need autoscale and burst policies.
[13:31] Alex: yep, autoscale and burst capacity supported for Hosted as a feature flag; for Dedicated we have more granular policies and guaranteed capacity.
[13:41] Derek: final — can we get a demo that shows a patient note query and an evidence snippet pulled up after rerank?
[13:48] Priya: yes, next demo we can build a hands-on notebook with patient note examples (synthetic) and structured evidence snippets.
[13:55] Alex: great. quick recap of next steps: send security pack + SOC2, notebook + API examples, schedule pilot planning, customer to share dataset.
[14:06] Maya: thanks — that covers it from us.
[14:10] Alex: thank you all. we'll follow up with the materials.
[14:14] [Call ends — small talk & goodbyes]

Notes on transcript: rough transcription; occasional mis-attributions and minor text artifacts from automatic captions. timestamps are approximate. The demo included a synthetic benchmark; production numbers vary.
